searchText: yes i can update -- what is it blocked on right now? i'll try to hop onto the call today, although i have a vet appt which probably lasts through the first 20 minutes I don't think that PR is blocked on anything ok sorry -- what is needed from me then? 😅 If you could address PR feedback, that would be great. I think outstanding are items from [review](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/7819#pullrequestreview-1721915436). Just pls double check my points and let me know if you have any doubt EOF call - https://www.google.com/url?q=https://us02web.zoom.us/j/88940506383?pwd%3DaTdsbHVyMTNDSUFHYmhTWlI2ZEVldz09&sa=D&source=calendar&usd=2&usg=AOvVaw0TYnvX2NE6cim9yG_bNNXU **EOF Implementers Meeting 33** https://youtu.be/fu0DLcgxF40 Nethermind's current EOF branch : https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/tree/Feature/EVM/EOF Hey there, I would like to know why in the Geth code got sometimes the Past EIPs with some `if` statements? I mean, is this possible that the nodes aren't running the same version but still sync together? (I suppose) Probably, with some *light* EIP (like only renaming OPInstruction etc should be working as this is not a breaking changes?). But in the case of **London** for example: Inside the code I can see this: ```golang var userRefund uint64 if !rules.IsLondon { // Before EIP-3529: refunds were capped to gasUsed / 2 userRefund = st.refundGas(params.RefundQuotient) } else { // After EIP-3529: refunds are capped to gasUsed / 5 userRefund = st.refundGas(params.RefundQuotientEIP3529) } ``` I would like to know the reason why we keep previous EIPs here (3529)? The following statement shouldn't be entering in this one right? (or this possible with old nodes somehow?) ``` // Before EIP-3529: refunds were capped to gasUsed / 2 ``` Maybe there is compatibility things I am probably missing here? if you got some example would be glad to hear more about it! https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/449d3f0d8799c0ae5a1d2629d89144058e69b5db/core/state_transition.go#L440-L440 It is needed for example for archive node sync and passing the tests that cover all past forks Oh yes! I forgot that ahah thanks does someone knows if there are a standart when **adding** a new instruction against modifying a previous Opcode during a new update here -> sometimes there is a `enableXXXX()` that modifying the Opcode. and sometimes like in the `newMergeInstructionSet()` there is a a adding like this? This is all very geth specific. I think you will get better answers from the Geth discord - https://discord.com/invite/nthXNEv Oh thanks!
